memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He is to take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense and take them behind the curtain. He is to put the incense on the fire before the LORD, and the smoke of the incense will conceal the atonement cover above the tablets of the covenant law, so that he will not die." - Lev 16:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Aaron steps behind the curtain — and immediately fills the room with smoke.

The incense is not decoration. It is protection. The cloud conceals the atonement cover so that he will not die. Even the high priest, on the holiest day, cleansed and carrying blood, could not look directly at the place where God's glory rested.

Moses once asked to see God's glory, and God said: you cannot see my face, for no one may see me and live (Ex 33:20). This is not a God we can casually examine.

And yet — hold this next to what John writes. No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son... has made him known (John 1:18). The invisible God has been made visible in Jesus.

Philip asked to be shown the Father, and Jesus answered: anyone who has seen me has seen the Father (John 14:9).

Where Aaron needed smoke to survive God's presence, we have been given a face. The glory that had to be veiled now looks at us with human eyes — the God who could not be seen, seen in Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What does God's unapproachable holiness stir in you?
2. How does it change things that God has made Himself known in Jesus?
3. Do you go to Christ when you want to know what God is like?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are holy beyond my seeing, and yet You have made Yourself known in Jesus. Thank You that I can look at Christ and see Your heart. Amen.
